reference_title: Design and Construction of Driven Pile Foundations

sections.title: Overview of Plan and Specification Requirements
sections.summary: Piles cannot be inspected after installation, so plans and specifications matter. Plans should list pile locations, numbering, type, toe and splice details, cutoff, cap connection, estimated and minimum toe elevations, batter, H-pile orientation, Rr, Rn, Rndr and borings; state the factored resistance, resistance factor, nominal resistance, unsuitable layer resistance, setup or relaxation and the resulting Rndr. Table 14-1 lists specification items.
sections.body: 14.1 Overview of Plan and Specification Requirements (pp. 281 to 283). Contract plans and specifications are the foundation designer's responsibility with materials and construction personnel. Plans should include: pile locations; a numbering system identifying each pile in a group or bent; type, section and estimated length; toe details (driving shoe, closure plate); splice details; cutoff elevation; cap connection details; estimated toe elevation; minimum toe elevation if needed; batter and direction; H-pile orientation; factored resistance Rr; nominal resistance Rn; nominal driving resistance Rndr; boring locations and exploration results. Language must be compatible, especially for the nominal driving resistance: 'piles shall have a resistance of 300 kips' could mean factored, nominal or nominal driving resistance, so plans should state the factored resistance, the resistance factor, the nominal resistance, the added resistance of unsuitable layers (scour, liquefaction and their elevations), post-driving changes (setup or relaxation) and the resulting Rndr. The chapter's generic specification (from FHWA Geotechnical Guideline 13, updated from ASD to LRFD; AASHTO LRFD Bridge Construction Specifications 2010 are similar) must be reviewed and modified before use; its commentary explains the provisions; it covers only driven piles. Design-bid-build uses agency standard specifications (agency takes the risk); design-build uses performance specifications (design-builder takes the risk); CM/GC uses standard specifications. Table 14-1 items: pile materials (type, grade, strength; coating; transportation and handling); driving system (hammer; hammer and pile cushions; helmet and inserts; leads; followers; predrilling, jetting and spudding equipment); installation (sequence; location and alignment tolerances; shoe or toe protection; splices; cutoff; cap connection; heave; rejection criteria); resistance verification (static, dynamic and rapid load testing; wave equation; dynamic formulas); payment (measurement; pay items).
key_points: Plans should show pile type, toe details, splices, cutoff and toe elevations, batter, Rr, Rn and Rndr
Avoid ambiguous 'resistance of 300 kips': state factored, nominal and nominal driving resistance
State the resistance factor, unsuitable-layer resistance and setup/relaxation behind Rndr
Generic specification (FHWA GT-13, now LRFD) must be reviewed and modified before use
Table 14-1: items a driven pile specification should include

tables.title: Items to Include in a Driven Pile Specification
tables.description: Pile materials (type, grade, strength; coatings; transportation and handling); driving system and equipment (hammer, hammer and pile cushions, helmet and inserts, leads, followers, predrilling, jetting, spudding); installation (sequence, location and alignment tolerances, shoes, splices, cutoff, cap connection, heave, rejection criteria); resistance verification (static, dynamic, rapid load testing, wave equation, dynamic formulas); basis of payment.

sections.title: Generic Driven Pile Specification
sections.summary: The generic driven pile specification's contents: X.01 Description; X.02 Submittals and Approvals (installation plan, equipment approval by wave equation or alternate method); X.03 Materials; X.04 Driving Equipment and Appurtenances; X.05 Determination of Nominal Resistance (compression, tension, lateral); X.06 Preparation and Driving; X.07 Method of Measurement; X.08 Basis of Payment.
sections.body: 14.2 Generic Driven Pile Specification (pp. 284 to 285). The specification opens with its contents list (pp. 284-285): X.01 Description (p. 286); X.02 Submittals and Approvals (p. 287): A pile installation plan, B pile driving equipment approval by wave equation, C approval by alternate method; X.03 Materials (p. 295); X.04 Driving Equipment and Appurtenances (p. 296): A pile hammers, B drive system components (hammer cushion, helmet, pile cushion, leads, followers, jets, predrilling equipment, spuds); X.05 Determination of Nominal Resistance (p. 303): A axial compression (static load tests, dynamic testing with signal matching, rapid load tests, wave equation analysis, dynamic formula), B axial tension (static load tests, dynamic testing with signal matching), C lateral resistance (static load tests); X.06 Preparation and Driving (p. 316): A site work, B preparation of piling, C driving (test, probe and indicator piles through unsatisfactory piles); X.07 Method of Measurement (p. 325): items A to P; X.08 Basis of Payment (p. 329).
key_points: Eight specification sections, X.01 Description to X.08 Basis of Payment (pp. 286-330)
Driving equipment is approved by wave equation analysis or by an alternate method (Section X.02)
Nominal resistance by static, dynamic, rapid load tests, wave equation or dynamic formula (Section X.05)
sections.applicability: The layout of a generic driven pile specification and where each provision sits.

sections.title: Section X.01 Description
sections.summary: Furnish and drive piles of the designated type to the location, elevation, penetration and/or nominal resistance shown; with test piles, plan lengths are estimates and the Engineer sets order lengths; perform specified load tests. The Owner estimates lengths and contractors should not be penalized for inaccurate estimates.
sections.body: 14.2.1 Section X.01 Description (p. 286). The item covers furnishing and driving foundation piles of the designated type and dimensions, including cutting off or building up, installed at the location and to the elevation, penetration and/or nominal resistance shown or as directed. Without test piles the Contractor furnishes the dimensions shown; with test piles, plan lengths are for estimating and the Engineer sets production lengths after test piles are driven and tested; order list lengths are those remaining after cutoff, and the Contractor adds length for fresh heading and its methods without compensation. Specified static, dynamic and/or rapid load tests are performed at the locations shown. Commentary: the Owner can assure proper installation and the Contractor expect equitable pay; the Owner estimates lengths for the nominal resistances from design-phase exploration, testing and analysis and expected variability; contractors should not be held accountable or indirectly penalized for inaccurate estimated lengths; the Contractor installs undamaged piles to the specified length, and the bid reflects cost and perceived risk.
key_points: With test piles, plan lengths are estimates; the Engineer sets order lengths
Owner is responsible for estimated pile lengths; contractors not penalized for inaccuracies
Contractor installs designated piles undamaged to the specified length
sections.applicability: Scope clause of a generic driven pile specification.

sections.title: Section X.02 Submittals and Approvals
sections.summary: Pile installation plan 30 days before driving (13 items). Equipment approved by wave equation (Pile and Driving Equipment Data Form, Figure 14-1): required blow count 30 to 96 blows/ft and stresses within phi_da limits (steel 0.90 fy; prestressed concrete tension 0.095 sqrt(f'c) + fpe, or fpe in severe corrosion, compression 0.85 f'c - fpe; timber 2.6 Fco; phi_da 1.0, timber 1.15). Table 14-2 resistance factors; alternate approval by rated energy (Table 14-3).
sections.body: 14.2.2 Section X.02 Submittals and Approvals (pp. 287 to 295). A) The Contractor submits a Pile Driving Installation Plan at least 30 days before driving: (1) equipment lists and hammer data sheets; (2) methods to determine field hammer energy, with calibrations; (3) follower and (4) template drawings; (5) load test equipment, instrumentation, procedures, reaction frame and pile arrangement and calibrations; (6) driving sequence; (7) schedule; (8) preconstruction survey and protection of nearby structures and utilities; (9) shop drawings; (10) preventing pile movement during fill placement within 15 ft; (11) placing reinforcement and concrete in pipe piles; (12) preventing batter pile deflection until the cap is cast; (13) splice locations and proprietary splices. B) Equipment approval is by wave equation unless a dynamic formula is specified; nothing is transported before written approval; the Pile and Driving Equipment Data Form (Figure 14-1) is submitted at least 30 days before driving, with follower drawings (commentary: wave equation approval cuts costs and claims; disputed rejections answered by a PE-sealed wave equation at the Contractor's cost; the form is used by the inspector even without wave equation approval). The required blow count at the required nominal resistance must be between 30 and 96 blows per foot (commentary: below practical refusal, 10 blows per inch). Stresses must not exceed phi_da limits (AASHTO 2014 phi_da = 1.0, timber 1.15): steel compression phi_da x 0.90 fy; prestressed concrete tension phi_da x (0.095 sqrt(f'c) + fpe) normally (ksi), phi_da x fpe in severe corrosive environments; compression phi_da x (0.85 f'c - fpe); timber compression phi_da x 2.6 Fco (AASHTO Table 8.4.1.4-1). Acceptance within 14 days, revisions within 7 days; unsuitable systems are modified at the Contractor's expense; changes need revised analyses and give no time extension. Commentary: Rndr is the resistance overcome (including unsuitable, liquefiable and scour zone soils) to reach the depth where the factored resistance is achieved with the field method's resistance factor; it depends on unsuitable layers, minimum penetration, temporary strength changes and installation methods (jetting, predrilling); it must be on the plans; optimum installation is below the bearing graph's maximum curvature (typically about 84 to 96 blows/ft). Table 14-2 (after AASHTO 2014): compression, static load test plus dynamic testing on at least 2 piles per site condition and 2% of production piles 0.80; static load test without dynamic testing 0.75; dynamic testing on 100% of piles 0.75; dynamic testing on 2 piles per site condition and 2% of piles 0.65; wave equation at end of drive 0.50; FHWA Modified Gates 0.40; Engineering News 0.10; tension, static load test 0.60, dynamic testing 0.50 (no AASHTO factor for rapid load tests, Section 11.4.7). C) Where a dynamic formula verifies resistance, hammers must have rated energy at least the Table 14-3 minimum for the nominal resistance (bands 180 and under, 181-300, 301-420, 421-540, 541-600, over 600 kips; values left for the agency) and the formula blow count must not exceed 10 blows per inch; the agency develops the table by wave equation (too large: stress problems or under 30 blows/ft; too small: over 120 blows/ft) for routine projects in uniform soils only.
key_points: Pile installation plan due 30 days before driving (13 required items)
Wave equation approval: 30 to 96 blows/ft at the required nominal resistance
Steel: compression <= phi_da x 0.90 fy (phi_da = 1.0; timber 1.15)
Prestressed concrete: tension <= phi_da (0.095 sqrt(f'c) + fpe); compression <= phi_da (0.85 f'c - fpe)
Timber: compression <= phi_da x 2.6 Fco
Alternate approval by minimum rated energy (Table 14-3) with formula blow count <= 10 blows/in.

tables.title: Resistance Factors for Field Determination Methods
tables.description: AASHTO compression phi_dyn: static load test on at least one pile per site condition plus dynamic testing with signal matching of at least two piles per site condition, not less than 2% of production piles, 0.80; static load test without dynamic testing 0.75; dynamic testing with signal matching on 100% of production piles 0.75; dynamic testing of at least two piles per site condition, not less than 2%, 0.65; wave equation alone at end of drive 0.50; FHWA modified Gates 0.40; Engineering News 0.10. Tension: static load test 0.60; dynamic testing with signal matching 0.50.

tables.title: Alternate Approval Method Minimum Pile Hammer Requirements
tables.description: Minimum manufacturer's rated hammer energy (ft-lbs) by nominal resistance bands of 180 kips and under, 181-300, 301-420, 421-540, 541-600 and over 600 kips; the energy column is left blank for each agency to fill from wave equation analyses (see commentary).

sections.applicability: Submittals, hammer approval criteria and resistance factors in a driven pile specification.

sections.title: Section X.03 Materials
sections.summary: Materials per the agency's standard specification subsections: portland cement concrete, reinforcing and prestressing steel, structural steel, shoe castings, cast-in-place shells, timber piles and treatment, protective coatings; see the AASHTO LRFD Bridge Construction Specifications (3rd Edition).
sections.body: 14.2.3 Section X.03 Materials (pp. 295 to 296). Materials meet subsections for portland cement concrete, reinforcing steel, prestressing strands and post-tensioning tendons, structural steel, castings for pile shoes, steel shells for cast-in-place piles, timber piles, timber preservative and treatment, and protective coatings. Commentary: insert the agency's standard specification sections; no generic materials section is possible given the combinations of materials and controls; adjust the list to the agency's specifications and pile type; the 3rd Edition AASHTO LRFD Bridge Construction Specifications add text and commentary on pile materials.
key_points: Materials clauses come from the agency's standard specifications
List: concrete, reinforcing/prestressing steel, structural steel, shoe castings, shells, timber, coatings
sections.applicability: Materials clause of a generic driven pile specification.

sections.title: Section X.04 Driving Equipment and Appurtenances
sections.summary: Hammers: drop hammers not for concrete piles or over 120 kips (ram >= 2.0 kips, drop <= 12 ft); air/steam striking parts >= 1/3 of helmet plus pile and >= 2.75 kips unless wave equation approved; OED stroke display; CED bounce chamber gauge; hydraulic energy readout; vibratory only after impact verification (restrike first of every 10). Hammer cushions: no wood, wire rope or asbestos, replace at 25% loss. Pile cushion new each pile, >= 4 in. with a formula. Followers, jets, predrilling, spuds.
sections.body: 14.2.4 Section X.04 Driving Equipment and Appurtenances (pp. 296 to 302). A) Air, steam, diesel or hydraulic hammers; drop hammers, if permitted, not for concrete piles or nominal resistance over 120 kips, ram at least 2.0 kips and not less than helmet plus pile, drop at most 12.0 ft, with guides. Air/steam hammers within manufacturer ranges with adequate plant, hose and accessible gauges; striking parts at least one third of helmet plus pile and at least 2.75 kips (waived with wave equation approval). Open end diesels: stroke rings, manufacturer's stroke-blow rate chart and an automatic stroke display device. Closed end diesels: bounce chamber gauge near ground and a chart calibrated within 60 days. Hydraulic hammers: field display of kinetic energy or impact velocity. Vibratory hammers for production piles only after toe elevation is set by load tests and/or impact restrikes at the Contractor's cost, controlled by power, penetration rate or toe elevation, with the first of every 10 piles restruck by impact. Commentary: inspectors need hammer manuals (Chapters 15 and 18; FHWA/RD 86/160; DFI guides); require kinetic energy readouts on large projects (Section 15.19); no formula predicts vibratory resistance (Section 7.10.5), so consider restrike dynamic testing. B) 1 Hammer cushion: durable manufactured material per the manufacturer; wood, wire rope and asbestos disallowed; striker plate; inspected at each structure start or every 100 hours; replaced when over 25% thinner. 2 Helmet: plane, guided by leads, no torsion; timber piles: least inside dimension within 2.0 in. of the head diameter; concrete heads plane and perpendicular. 3 Pile cushion: same area as the concrete pile top, plywood or hardwood, thickness by wave equation (at least 4 in. with a dynamic formula), new for each pile, replaced if compressed over half or burning, kept dry; used cushion (the end of driving one) for restrikes (commentary: thicknesses over 18 in. used for tension; wood hardens after about 1000 to 1500 blows; cushions with fewer than 50 blows unsuitable for restrikes). 4 Leads: fixed or swinging (embedded or templated, pile gate), long enough to avoid followers. 5 Followers only if approved, with wave equation; steel follower area at least 20% of a concrete pile's, impedance 50 to 200% of steel or timber piles; first two piles checked (commentary: erratic energy loss, check by static or dynamic testing). 6 Jets only if approved; removed 5 ft above minimum toe elevation, then impact driven; restrikes of jetted groups. 7 Predrilling (commentary: smaller than pile diagonal for alignment, heave or vibration; up to largest pile dimension plus 6 in. for embankments or obstructions; backfill with sand, pea gravel or grout). 8 Spuds to displace obstructions.
key_points: Drop hammers: not for concrete piles or Rn > 120 kips; ram >= 2.0 kips; drop <= 12 ft
Air/steam striking parts >= 1/3 of helmet + pile and >= 2.75 kips (unless wave equation approved)
OED stroke display, CED bounce chamber gauge, hydraulic energy readout required
Vibratory production piles: first of every 10 restruck with an impact hammer
Hammer cushion: no wood, wire rope or asbestos; replace if > 25% thinner
Pile cushion: new each pile; >= 4 in. with a dynamic formula; replace if compressed > 1/2
Steel follower: area >= 20% of concrete pile; impedance 50 to 200% for steel/timber piles
Jets removed 5 ft above the minimum toe elevation; finish with impact driving
sections.applicability: Hammer and drive system requirements in a driven pile specification.

sections.title: Section X.05 Determination of Nominal Resistance
sections.summary: Compression: static test per ASTM D1143 quick method to plunging (150% loading capacity), failure sf = Delta + (0.15 + b/120) for b <= 24 in. (Eq. 14-1), Delta + b/30 over 36 in. (Eq. 14-2), interpolated between; dynamic testing per ASTM D4945 with restrike (Table 14-4 delays); rapid tests per ASTM D7383; wave equation; Modified Gates (Eqs. 14-3 to 14-5) up to 600 kips. Tension: ASTM D3689, sf = Delta + 0.15 (Eq. 14-6). Lateral: ASTM D3966 to 200%.
sections.body: 14.2.5 Section X.05 Determination of Nominal Resistance (pp. 303 to 316). A) Axial compression, by: 1 Static load tests per ASTM D1143 quick method to geotechnical plunging failure or system capacity, loading system 150% of nominal resistance, load cell and spherical bearing plate, PE-prepared apparatus plans, calibrations within 30 days; reaction piles of production type, redriven if permanently raised 0.25 in. or more; no timber or tapered reaction piles in permanent locations. Failure is the load giving head movement sf = Delta + (0.15 + b/120) for piles 24 in. or less (Eq. 14-1; Delta elastic deformation of total pile length, b diameter or side, in inches), sf = Delta + b/30 for piles over 36 in. (Eq. 14-2), with linear interpolation for 24 to 36 in. Re-drive if heave exceeds 1/4 in.; test no sooner than 5 days after driving; cut off unused piles 1 ft below footing or grade. Commentary: test after equilibrium (clays at least 2 weeks, sandy silts and sands 5 days to a week, shales at least 2 weeks; Section 7.2.4); measure toe load (strain gages, telltales); jack gauges read 10 to 20% high from ram friction; add reporting sections when the Contractor's firm tests; state review time (Chapter 9). 2 Dynamic testing with signal matching per ASTM D4945 at end of initial driving and each restrike (commentary: ASTM D4945 alone is insufficient; PDCA/PDI proficiency levels; test half the reaction piles and the load test pile, and restrike it after the static test; 2 piles per site condition and 2% up to 100%, Section 10.3). Gages 2 to 3 diameters below the head; 4 x 4 ft manlift; about 1 hour per pile; 10 amp, 115 volt power; 8 x 8 ft shelter on barges; stresses held to X.02 B limits; restrike after up to 24 hours (or Table 14-4) with a warmed hammer (20 blows), at most 3 in. or 20 blows. Table 14-4 restrike delays: clean sands 1 day, silty sands 2, sandy silts 3-5, silty clays 7-14, shales 10-14 days (longer sometimes); too short a delay causes overruns; state analysis time. 3 Rapid load tests per ASTM D7383 (combustion gas or cushioned drop weight); peak force over target resistance plus dynamic resistance, pulse above 50% of peak for 4L/C and above static pre-load for at least 12L/C (less with added gages); load cell 10% over peak; interpretation with stated loading rate reduction factor; no sooner than 5 days (commentary: Sections 11.4.1-11.4.5; no AASHTO resistance factor, Section 11.4.7). 4 Wave equation: penetration resistance reached within 5 ft of the estimated toe elevation. 5 Dynamic formula only if specified, not over 600 kips, not with damaged heads or followers: Modified Gates Rndr = 1.75 sqrt(Ed) log10(10 Nb) - 100 (Eq. 14-3; Ed = W h in ft-lbs during the observed set, Nb blows/in.), Nft = 12 (10^x) (Eq. 14-4), x = [(Rndr + 100)/(1.75 sqrt(Ed))] - 1 (Eq. 14-5). Commentary: set criteria for the nominal driving resistance including unsuitable layers and minimum toe elevations; FHWA recommends wave equation over formulas (Chapter 12). B) Axial tension: 1 static tests per ASTM D3689, failure at upward movement sf = Delta + (0.15) (Eq. 14-6; Delta elastic lengthening), factored by phi_up from Table 14-2; 2 dynamic testing: restrike signal matching shaft resistance times phi_up. C) Lateral: ASTM D3966 standard procedure to 200% of design lateral load (one standard, 7 optional procedures), deflection versus depth by in-place inclinometers or Shape Accel Array.
key_points: Compression failure: sf = Delta + (0.15 + b/120) for b <= 24 in. (Eq. 14-1)
Large piles (> 36 in.): sf = Delta + b/30 (Eq. 14-2); interpolate for 24 to 36 in.
Static tests no sooner than 5 days; clays and shales at least 2 weeks recommended
Restrike delays (Table 14-4): sands 1 day to shales 10-14 days
Rapid load test pulse > 50% of peak for 4L/C and above static preload for >= 12L/C
Wave equation criterion met within 5 ft of estimated toe elevation
Modified Gates (Eqs. 14-3 to 14-5) only if specified, <= 600 kips
Tension failure: sf = Delta + 0.15 in. (Eq. 14-6), times phi_up
Lateral load tests per ASTM D3966 to 200% of design load

tables.title: Common Time Delay for Restrike Based Upon Soil Type
tables.description: Restrike delay by soil type: clean sands 1 day; silty sands 2 days; sandy silts 3-5 days; silty clays 7-14 days; shales 10-14 days (longer times sometimes required for the last two).

sections.applicability: Specifying how nominal resistance is verified in compression, tension and lateral loading.

sections.title: Section X.06 Preparation and Driving
sections.summary: Site work, predrilling (stop 5 ft above plan toe except end bearing; embankments over 5 ft; hole <= pile dimension + 6 in.), pile preparation (collars over 200 kips timber; cast steel shoes; marking), test piles (set up 12-24 h), production piles, sequence, tolerances (0.25 in./ft vertical, 0.5 in./ft batter; 6 in., 3 in. bents), heave (0.25 in. end bearing, 1.5 in. friction), refusal (10 blows/in. for 3 in.; 20 blows for 1 in.), splices, cutoff, unsatisfactory piles.
sections.body: 14.2.6 Section X.06 Preparation and Driving (pp. 316 to 325). A) Site work: 1 excavate to grade before driving; fill placed and settled before driving at abutments (piles first only where minimal settlement is expected). 2 Predrilling as specified, then impact driving to criteria, voids filled with sand; no spuds in lieu (commentary: except end bearing piles, stop at least 5 ft above plan toe; to rock or hardpan for end bearing); disturbed piles redriven, at the Contractor's cost unless the method was specified. 3 Predrilling through compacted fill or embankments over 5 ft, diameter at most the greatest pile dimension plus 6 in. B) Preparation: 1 heads plane and perpendicular, strands cut below the surface, concrete and timber heads chamfered; 2 timber collars or bands over 200 kips; 3 shoes of cast steel ASTM A148 (Grade 90-60) for H-piles and open pipes, closure plates A36 or better (commentary: welded plate H-pile shoes not recommended, Chapter 16); 4 marking at 1 ft with cumulative distance every 5 ft, inch marks over 10 ft if directed. C) Driving: 1 test, probe and indicator piles first, slightly longer than production; not reaching Rndr 1 ft above estimated toe, set up 12 to 24 hours and redrive with a warmed hammer (20 blows), splice if needed; record blows per foot and per inch near the end and in the first foot of redrive; order list within 7 days (commentary: recommended for long friction piles, large resistance relative to load, concrete piles). 2 Production piles to nominal resistance, plus minimum toe elevation, or designated toe elevation, documenting blow count and stroke, velocity or blow rate; jetted piles judged on post-jetting impact driving; follower criteria verified by static or dynamic testing; vibratory piles: first of each ten impact driven, remaining nine to similar toe, power and rate; hammer approval does not relieve damage responsibility. 3 Driving stresses within X.02 B. 4 Sequence: from the center outward or from one side across. 5 Tolerances: 0.25 in./ft (1:50) from vertical, 0.5 in./ft (1:25) from batter; head within 6 in. of plan (3 in. for bents); at least 4 in. from cap edges; cutoff 1.5 in. above to 4 in. below plan, at least 8 in. embedment; overloading evaluated, redesign at the Contractor's cost (commentary: sloping bedrock cases; tolerances of 3 in. or less impractical). 6 Heave: redrive end bearing piles over 0.25 in., shaft resistance piles over 1.5 in.; paid if sequence followed. 7 Unforeseeable obstructions paid. 8 Practical refusal 10 blows per inch for at most 3 consecutive inches; absolute refusal 20 blows for 1 in. or less; on hard rock 5 blows per 1/4 in. or 10 blows per 1/2 in.; at maximum fuel or stroke unless approved lower (commentary: warranties void above 10 blows per inch for 6 to 12 in. or 20 blows per inch for more than 1 in.; avoid extended driving above 10 blows per inch). 9 Splices: full length wherever practical, never splice timber; steel per AWS D1.1 by certified welders, unwelded mechanical splices only for compression piles. 10 Cutoff; treated timber cut areas with copper naphthenate (at least 2% copper); marine timber capped. 11 Unsatisfactory piles: a concrete pile with a crack around the entire periphery is defective; remedies by replacement, adjacent piles, build-ups, extended footings or added cap steel.
key_points: Predrilling stops at least 5 ft above plan toe (except end bearing); hole <= pile dimension + 6 in.
Test piles not reaching Rndr: set up 12 to 24 hours, then redrive with a warmed hammer
Tolerances: 0.25 in./ft vertical, 0.5 in./ft batter; head within 6 in. (3 in. for bents)
Cutoff 1.5 in. above to 4 in. below plan; at least 8 in. cap embedment
Redrive heaved piles: > 0.25 in. end bearing, > 1.5 in. shaft resistance
Practical refusal 10 blows/in. for 3 in.; absolute refusal 20 blows for <= 1 in.
Hard rock: 5 blows per 1/4 in. or 10 blows per 1/2 in.
Never splice timber piles; unwelded mechanical splices only for compression piles
Concrete pile with a crack around the entire periphery is defective
sections.applicability: Installation, tolerance, heave and refusal clauses of a driven pile specification.

sections.title: Section X.07 Method of Measurement
sections.summary: Measurement items A to P: mobilization lump sum (75% at start of satisfactory driving, 25% at completion); piles and test piles furnished and driven per foot or each; static, dynamic (driving or restrike), rapid and lateral load tests each; splices only beyond plan lengths; shoes; predrilling; jetting; cutoff; spudding; delays and rig moves by time.
sections.body: 14.2.7 Section X.07 Method of Measurement (pp. 325 to 329). A) Mobilization: lump sum, 75% when equipment is mobilized and satisfactory driving has begun, 25% on completion; labor of manipulating equipment is in the pile unit price. B) Piles furnished per linear foot or each, including approved extensions, not replacements of accepted piles damaged later. C) Piles driven per foot or each, including all related costs not otherwise paid. D) Test piles furnished and E) driven likewise. F) Static load tests per completed test, reaction and test piles not in the structure included; Contractor-option tests not paid. G) Dynamic tests (during driving or restrike) each, plus the applicable pile items; unspecified tests needing repositioning or delay (e.g., a second longer term restrike at the owner's request) paid per hour. H) Rapid load tests each, including site preparation. I) Lateral load tests each (a two-pile push or pull is one test). J) Splices only where required beyond plan estimated lengths. K) Pile shoes installed (or within the furnished pile price if stated). L) Predrilling, M) jetting, N) cutoff (including disposal), O) spudding, P) delays, downtime or out of sequence moves caused by the owner, recorded per occurrence.
key_points: Mobilization: 75% when satisfactory driving starts, 25% at completion
Separate items for piles furnished and piles driven (per foot or each)
Splices paid only when required beyond plan estimated lengths
Owner-caused delays and out-of-sequence moves measured by time
sections.applicability: Measurement clauses of a driven pile specification.

sections.title: Section X.08 Basis of Payment
sections.summary: Pay items and units (Table 14-5): mobilization lump sum; piles and test piles furnished and driven per linear foot or each; load tests, splices, shoes and cutoffs (over 5 ft only) each; predrilling and jetting per foot or each; spudding and delays per hour. Separate fixed-cost items and furnished/driven items treat length overruns and underruns equitably.
sections.body: 14.2.8 Section X.08 Basis of Payment (pp. 329 to 330). Accepted quantities are paid at contract unit prices for each pile size and type as full compensation. Table 14-5 (pay item: unit): mobilization and demobilization: lump sum; piles furnished, piles driven, test pile furnished, test pile driven: linear foot or each; static load test, dynamic pile test (during driving), dynamic pile test (during restrike), rapid load test, lateral load test, pile splices, pile shoes: each; predrilling, jetting: linear foot or each; pile cut-off (over 5 ft lengths only): each; spudding (punching), delays, downtime or out-of-sequence moves: per hour. Commentary: separating major fixed costs from variable costs avoids folding mobilization, splices and shoes into a per-foot price, which under-recovers costs on underruns and overpays on overruns; ordered length is the agency's responsibility, and separate furnished and driven items pay actual materials and installation even with modest overruns or underruns.
